issues.title: Review deterministic candidate-ranking tie-break changes
issues.author: altanai
issues.body:
Track review of the deterministic ranking additions in the draft.

Scope:
- Review adding the transcript digest after Ni, Nr, SPIi, and SPIr in the candidate ranking tuple.
- Validate the digest input definition and ensure both peers derive identical bytes for the same successful IKE_SA_INIT exchange.
- Review duplicate-candidate handling and the rule against local timestamps, unique IDs, or arrival order as tie-breaks.
- Identify needed clarifications, security considerations, and examples for equal-field cases.

Done when the ranking procedure and edge cases have been reviewed and any resulting draft edits are recorded.

comments.author: altanai
comments.body:
The aim is , if one peer finishes authenticating a candidate before the other, it should defer deleting the current winner until both peers know the competing candidate is eligible.

My current draft compare the ranks 
```
winner = max(Rank(X), Rank(Y))
Rank = (Ni, Nr, SPIi, SPIr, TD)

where 
- Ni and Nr  the nonce sent by the IKE_SA_INIT initiator and  IKE_SA_INIT responder respectively
- SPIi  and   SPIr are the initiator’s and responder’s IKE Security Parameter Index.
- TD is the transcript digest: SHA-256(IKE_SA_INIT request || IKE_SA_INIT response), using the encoded IKE messages, excluding IP/UDP headers.
```

So to make the ranking deterministic, here are some options 

a. RTT-based holdoff like wait a multiple of measures RTT before initiation IKE DEL

b. Configure the same peer as the preferred cleanup peer then use the existing rank tuple to break ties between its attempts ( dont want this because the other end may get stalled waiting which brings us back to square one)

c. This is ambitious but the best approach IMO. Explicitly exchange collision-group and candidate-status information. May become a tough since both peers need to support the opt-in extension.

d. same as c but using standard INFORMATIONAL and DELETE exchanges, with a holdoff for in-flight attempts. Little complex but Im sure brainstorming would help here.

issues.title: Compare Libreswan and strongSwan simultaneous IKEv2 collision behavior
issues.author: altanai
issues.body:
Compare Libreswan and strongSwan behavior for simultaneous IKE SA initiation and overlapping CREATE_CHILD_SA exchanges.

Investigate:
- Which IKE SAs and Child SAs each implementation retains after simultaneous initiation.
- How each implementation handles inbound and outbound traffic when policy state is associated with different SAs.
- What happens during loser cleanup, including DELETE ordering, SPD policy migration, and recovery if deletion fails.
- Whether observed behavior differs by implementation version or configuration.

Record versions, configurations, packet or event traces, resulting SA and policy state, and traffic continuity. Summarize the differences and feed relevant findings back into the draft.

comments.author: altanai
comments.body:
Found relevant Libreswan prior art that should be included in this comparison ( thanks to Ondrej Moris): 

- [Issue #2445: “IKE_AUTH requests crossed”](https://github.com/libreswan/libreswan/issues/2445) describes simultaneous IKE_SA_INIT and IKE_AUTH exchanges. Both peers respond to the other’s IKE_AUTH, establish responder-side IKE and Child SAs, then discard their locally initiated IKE SAs while IKE_AUTH is still outstanding. The reported result can be mismatched Child SAs at the two ends.
- [PR #2447: “detect and resolve simultaneous IKE_AUTH exchanges”](https://github.com/libreswan/libreswan/pull/2447) added an opt-in resolution for this case on the same permanent connection. When processing an IKE_AUTH as responder, Libreswan checks for a competing locally initiated IKE SA with IKE_AUTH outstanding. If that competing SA completed IKE_AUTH within the preceding second, it keeps that SA and rejects the current responder exchange; otherwise, it compares the initiator nonces and keeps the SA with the higher nonce. It rejects the losing responder exchange with AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, or terminates the local losing initiator SA. The behavior is disabled by default and enabled with `reject-simultaneous-ike-auth=yes`.

This is useful implementation prior art, but its recovery relies on permanent connections and their revival behavior, so it does not directly cover instantiated/on-demand connections where revival cannot be assumed. The PR is specifically about crossed IKE_AUTH handling; our comparison should also test overlapping CREATE_CHILD_SA exchanges and examine SPD/policy migration and traffic continuity during cleanup. Compare Libreswan configuration (including the opt-in setting) against strongSwan around this use case

issues.title: Document simultaneous IKE_SA_INIT, IKE_AUTH, and DELETE call flows
issues.author: altanai
issues.body:
Create dedicated message-sequence diagrams for races spanning simultaneous IKE_SA_INIT, IKE_AUTH completion, and incoming or crossed DELETE messages.

Start with cases where both peers initiate IKE_SA_INIT and end up with multiple candidates. Cover interleavings where:
- A second authenticated candidate arrives before, during, or just after local processing of the final IKE_AUTH message.
- DELETE arrives before, during, or just after the peer processes IKE_AUTH.
- A DELETE crosses with the final IKE_AUTH message, or both peers initiate cleanup.
- One peer has one authenticated candidate while the other has two.
- A DELETE is duplicated, delayed, or received after a candidate has become the selected winner.

For each flow, show message ordering, per-peer state transitions, candidate status, DELETE handling, traffic publication, and SPD ownership. State the expected convergence behavior and whether traffic can experience a one-way leak or a traffic hole.

issues.title: Map Child SA races across competing parent IKE SAs
issues.author: altanai
issues.body:
Document how Child SA creation interacts with competing parent IKE SAs during simultaneous initiation.

Enumerate cases where:
- CREATE_CHILD_SA begins under one parent while a second IKE_SA_INIT/IKE_AUTH candidate is still in progress.
- Child SA exchanges are initiated or received under different parent IKE SAs.
- IKE_AUTH completion or parent-SA arbitration changes which parent is selected while a Child SA exchange is underway.
- A parent is deleted or loses arbitration while its Child SA exchange is pending or completes late.

For each case, show the parent/Child SA association, state transitions, candidate grouping and cleanup. Identify the protocol rules needed to avoid orphaned Child SAs, duplicate tunnels, or inconsistent winner decisions.

issues.title: Model split inbound and outbound forwarding during collision cleanup
issues.author: altanai
issues.body:
Model and validate the split-forwarding case where inbound traffic uses one Child SA while outbound traffic uses another.

Trace policy and dataplane state before, during, and after loser cleanup, including SPD ownership and any migration from the losing SA to the retained SA. Define the install/remove ordering and analyze packet loss, a traffic hole, or a one-way leak during cutover. Record a reproducible scenario and observed traffic/state evidence. Use issue #2 for cross-implementation comparison; this issue focuses on the forwarding model and cutover safety.

pulls.title: Add IKEv2 Child SA collision call flows
pulls.author: altanai
pulls.body:
Added flows showing how simultaneous IKE_SA_INIT and the point at which authenticated Child SAs become eligible for arbitration. There is also a walk through a lost IKE_AUTH response and explaination on  why the example defers cleanup while the peers have different eligible candidate sets.

Show one-sided and crossed Child SA Deletes, including which SPIs appear in the requests and responses under RFC 7296, Section 1.4.1.

The examples treat candidate-set agreement as an explicit condition. The draft still leaves its wire encoding and acknowledgement rules open.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Rendered all four sequence diagrams with Pandoc and checked lifeline alignment.
- Checked the Child SA Delete flows against RFC 7296, Section 1.4.1.
